message.content:
### Building a New PC – Step‑by‑Step Guide

Below is a practical, beginner‑friendly walkthrough.  
Feel free to skip sections you already know, but keep the order for safety and best results.

| # | What to Do | Why It Matters | Tips |
|---|------------|----------------|------|
| 1 | **Plan & Budget** | Know what you’ll use it for (gaming, video editing, office, etc.) | Use PCPartPicker to check compatibility and price. |
| 2 | **Gather Tools & Workspace** | A clean, static‑free area keeps components safe. | 1 × Phillips screwdriver, anti‑static wrist strap, plenty of light. |
| 3 | **Choose a Case** | Determines airflow, size, and aesthetics. | ATX mid‑tower is most common; make sure it fits your motherboard form factor. |
| 4 | **Pick a Motherboard** | The hub that connects everything. | Match socket to CPU (e.g., Intel LGA 1200, AMD AM4). |
| 5 | **Select a CPU** | Drives performance. | Consider core count, clock speed, and budget. |
| 6 | **Get RAM** | Fast memory improves multitasking. | DDR4/DDR5, 16 GB minimum for gaming, 32 GB+ for content creation. |
| 7 | **Choose Storage** | SSDs are fast; HDDs add bulk. | NVMe M.2 SSD for OS + games, SATA SSD/HDD for bulk. |
| 8 | **Pick a GPU** | Essential for gaming, video rendering. | Balance with CPU; avoid bottlenecks. |
| 9 | **Select Power Supply (PSU)** | Supplies power safely. | 80+ Bronze or better, 650 W+ for mid‑range builds. |
| 10 | **Install CPU** | Core of the system. | Align pin/land pattern, apply thermal paste, attach cooler. |
| 11 | **Mount Motherboard in Case** | Securely positions all components. | Use standoffs, screw firmly, avoid touching contacts. |
| 12 | **Install RAM** | Slot into DIMM slots. | Insert at angle, lock in place. |
| 13 | **Mount Storage** | SSD/HDD in drive bays or M.2 slot. | Secure with screws or tool‑free brackets. |
| 14 | **Install GPU** | Slot into PCI‑e x16. | Secure with screws, connect power cables. |
| 15 | **Attach PSU** | Connect to motherboard, GPU, storage, case fans. | Route cables neatly, use cable ties. |
| 16 | **Connect Case Fans & Front Panel** | Power, USB, audio, power button. | Refer to motherboard manual for exact pins. |
| 17 | **Check All Connections** | Prevent shorts, ensure power flow. | Double‑check every cable, no loose screws. |
| 18 | **First Boot** | Verify hardware recognition. | Enter BIOS/UEFI, set boot order, check temperatures. |
| 19 | **Install Operating System** | Windows, Linux, etc. | Create bootable USB, follow installer prompts. |
| 20 | **Install Drivers & Updates** | Ensure hardware works optimally. | Download latest GPU drivers, chipset drivers, Windows updates. |
| 21 | **Test & Benchmark** | Confirm stability, performance. | Use 3DMark, Cinebench, or simple stress tests. |
| 22 | **Cable Management & Final Clean‑up** | Improves airflow, looks tidy. | Trim excess cable length, secure with ties. |
| 23 | **Enjoy & Maintain** | Keep system running smoothly. | Clean dust filters, update drivers, monitor temperatures. |

---

#### Quick Checklist

- **Case** – ATX mid‑tower, good airflow
- **Motherboard** – ATX, correct socket, enough PCI‑e slots
- **CPU** – Core count, clock speed, socket match
- **RAM** – 16 GB DDR4/DDR5, dual‑channel
- **Storage** – NVMe SSD (500 GB+) + optional SATA HDD
- **GPU** – Mid‑range or high‑end depending on use
- **PSU** – 80+ Bronze, 650 W+, modular if possible
- **Cooling** – Stock cooler or aftermarket air/ liquid cooler
- **Tools** – Phillips screwdriver, anti‑static wrist strap

---

#### Common Pitfalls & How to Avoid Them

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| **Shorted motherboard** | Use standoffs, never touch CPU pins, keep case open until all components are installed. |
| **Overheating** | Ensure proper airflow, use quality thermal paste, keep fans balanced. |
| **Bottleneck** | Pair CPU & GPU appropriately; avoid a weak CPU with a strong GPU or vice versa. |
| **Power issues** | Verify PSU wattage, use a PSU calculator, double‑check all power connectors. |
| **Driver conflicts** | Install chipset drivers first, then GPU, then other peripherals. |

---

#### Resources

- **PCPartPicker** – Build planner, compatibility checker, price tracking.  
- **YouTube Channels** – Linus Tech Tips, JayzTwoCents, Paul's Hardware for visual guides.  
- **Reddit** – r/buildapc for community support, troubleshooting.  
- **Manuals** – Keep motherboard, case, PSU manuals handy; they contain pinouts and diagrams.

---

### Final Thought

Building a PC is a rewarding project that gives you control over performance, aesthetics, and future upgrades. Take your time, double‑check every connection, and enjoy the process! If you hit a snag, feel free to ask for help—happy building!
